blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
The balance sheet is a photograph of a company at a single moment. It shows everything the company owns. We call these things assets. It also shows everything the company owes. We call these liabilities. What is left for the owners is called equity.

The two sides must always match. Assets are equal to liabilities plus equity. This is always true.

The income statement, or P&L, tells you what happened during a period. The balance sheet tells you where the company stands right now. Together, they answer two different questions: how are we doing, and where are we?

items.q: What does the balance sheet show?
options: A photograph of the company at one moment
The names of all the workers
items.why: "The balance sheet is a photograph of a company at a single moment."

items.q: What do we call the things the company owns?
items.why: "It shows everything the company owns. We call these things assets."

items.q: The two sides of the balance sheet must always…
items.why: "The two sides must always match. Assets are equal to liabilities plus equity."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which idea?
options: The balance sheet shows one moment.
The balance sheet and the P&L answer the same question.
Equity is what is left for the owners.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que os dois relatórios respondem a perguntas diferentes.

items.q: The text suggests that the P&L and the balance sheet are…
items.why: Inferência: "Together, they answer two different questions" — juntos, se complementam.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie explicando a um novo colega. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Welcome to the team! Let me help you with these two reports. People often mix them up, so this is important.

Think of the balance sheet as a photo. It is one moment in time. It shows what we own today and what we owe today. The two sides always match. That is the rule.

Now think of the P&L as a film. It tells a story over time. It shows the sales and the costs during the month or the year. It is about action, not a single moment.

So the balance sheet asks: where are we right now? The P&L asks: how are we doing over time? Two very different questions. You need both to see the full picture.

Here at Czarnikow, we prepare the balance sheet at the end of every quarter. When you read it, you can see the health of the company at that date. Don't worry — after a few weeks, this will feel very natural. Come to me any time with your questions.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Sophie describe the balance sheet?
options: As a photo of one moment
As a plan for the future
items.why: "Think of the balance sheet as a photo. It is one moment in time."

items.q: How does Sophie describe the P&L?
options: As a film that tells a story over time
items.why: "Now think of the P&L as a film. It tells a story over time."

items.q: When does Czarnikow prepare the balance sheet?
options: At the end of every quarter
items.why: "Here at Czarnikow, we prepare the balance sheet at the end of every quarter."

items.q: Why does Sophie explain the two reports so carefully?
options: Because people often mix them up
Because the new colleague is a manager
Because they are the same report
items.why: Inferência: "People often mix them up, so this is important."

items.q: What is Sophie's attitude to the new colleague?
items.why: Inferência: ela dá as boas-vindas e diz "Come to me any time with your questions."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The company's cars and computers are assets." An asset is something the company…
items.why: Asset = ativo: algo que a empresa possui.

items.q: "The loan from the bank is a liability." A liability is something the company…
items.why: Liability = passivo: uma dívida, algo que a empresa deve.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The money left for the owners is called ___."
items.why: Equity = patrimônio: o que sobra para os donos.

items.q: "The two sides of the report always match." To match means to…
items.why: To match = bater, coincidir: os dois lados são iguais.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The balance sheet shows the ___ of the company right now."
items.why: Position = posição: onde a empresa está neste momento.

blocks.instruction: Expressões simples de trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Don't mix up the two reports." To mix up means to…
items.why: Mix up = confundir uma coisa com a outra.

items.q: "The manager must sign off on the report." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar, dar o aval.

items.q: "Let me walk you through the balance sheet." To walk someone through means to…
items.why: Walk you through = explicar passo a passo.

items.q: "Can you fill in for me at the meeting?" To fill in means to…
items.why: Fill in = substituir alguém, cobrir a ausência.

items.q: "After a few weeks, you will pick it up." To pick something up means to…
items.why: Pick it up = aprender, pegar o jeito.
